name: LRU cache
brief: A cache of at most `capacity` keys. `get(k)` returns the value or -1, and counts as a use. `put(k, v)` stores or updates `k`, also a use. When the cache is over capacity, drop the least recently used key. Both calls take constant time on average.
constraints: Capacity may be 0: then nothing is stored.
A `put` of an existing key updates the value and counts as a use.
hint: Keep a `std::list` of (key, value) pairs, most recent first, and an `unordered_map` from key to list iterator. `splice` moves a node to the front without allocating.

examples.name: A get saves a key
examples.note: get 1 makes key 1 recent, so adding key 3 drops key 2.

tests.name: A get saves a key
tests.note: get 1 makes key 1 recent, so adding key 3 drops key 2.

how: Seven hidden tests drive the cache with puts and gets: eviction order, capacity 1 and 0, updates and many keys. A hidden driver calls `put` and `get` and compares every result of `get`.
notes: Move a key to the front on every `get` and every `put`.
Evict from the back of the list, and erase the key from the map as well.
